images.note: Thomas Jefferson; beat: strict-construction dilemma, drafted-then-shelved amendment, 'in his own hand' 1803 letter. Primary: silver relief by Johann Mathias Reich, 1801 (contemporary, painted from life era). Alt: stipple engraving 1802 after Gilbert Stuart (contemporary).
images.title: Thomas Jefferson, silver relief portrait by Johann Mathias Reich, 1801

images.note: Napoleon Bonaparte; beat: strong-armed Spain into retroceding Louisiana, sent Leclerc to Saint-Domingue, put Louisiana on the market. Primary: oil on wood, French painter, undated (honest: no date on record). Alt: stipple print by M. Mercoli after L. Bacler d'Albe, Napoleon's own map-maker (Napoleonic era).
images.title: Napoleon Bonaparte, oil portrait by French painter (undated)

images.alt_source: Library of Congress (item 2014645197, Toussaint L Overture portrait print)
images.note: Toussaint Louverture; beat: leader of the 1791 slave revolt, seized summer 1802, died at Fort de Joux April 1803. Pen-and-ink drawing by Claude Louis Desrais, ca. 1802 — drawn during Louverture's lifetime (contemporary). No qualifying second-institution image found (LOC's c1870 chromolithograph only 785px wide).
images.title: Toussaint Louverture on Horseback, pen and ink by Claude Louis Desrais, ca. 1802

images.alt_source: Library of Congress (https://www.loc.gov/item/2003677110/ - James Monroe engraving, 1828)
images.note: James Monroe; beat: envoy sent after Livingston, authorized $10M for New Orleans and West Florida, signed for everything. Oil by Gilbert Stuart, ca. 1820-22 (near-contemporary, from life). No qualifying second-institution image found (LOC holdings are late copies or undigitized).
images.title: James Monroe, oil portrait by Gilbert Stuart, ca. 1820-22

images.note: Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Perigord; beat: Napoleon's foreign minister who asked 'what will you give for all of Louisiana'. Oil by Baron Francois Gerard, 1808 (near-contemporary, 5 years after the purchase). No qualifying second-institution image (LOC's 1814 print only 762px wide).
images.title: Talleyrand, Prince de Benevent, oil portrait by Baron Francois Gerard, 1808

images.alt_source: Boston Public Library / Digital Commonwealth - Louisiana map, 1804 (commonwealth:9s161b33m)
images.note: Louisiana territory; beat: $15M for 828,000 sq mi, 'three cents an acre', doubled the country; fuzzy borders that festered until Adams-Onis 1819. Period map titled 'Louisiana', 1805 (contemporary, 2 years after purchase), Library of Congress Geography & Map Division. No firmly-dated second-institution period map found.
images.title: Louisiana (map), 1805

images.note: Corps of Discovery; beat: 1804-1806 up the Missouri, across the Rockies, to the Pacific; 'mapping it was claiming it' — the expedition told Britain and Spain the land was claimed. 'A map of Lewis and Clark's track... by order of the executive of the United States in 1804, 5 & 6' (published with the 1814 journals from expedition surveys; later printing of contemporary surveys). No second-institution copy found.
images.title: A map of Lewis and Clark's track across North America, 1804-1806 (1814 journal map)
